gallery.filename: Inside the 'Picture House', Ulster Folk Museum - geograph.org.uk - 1107590.jpg
gallery.title: File:Inside the 'Picture House', Ulster Folk Museum - geograph.org.uk - 1107590.jpg
gallery.description: Inside the 'Picture House', Ulster Folk Museum The 'Picture House' in the Ulster Folk Museum is a replica of one which stood in Gilford, County Armagh. It ran as a silent cinema from c1909-c1931. Showing here was a Charlie Chaplin picture.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland
Taken with Canon PowerShot S5 IS

gallery.description: Milestone, Ulster Folk Museum An old milestone that has been relocated to the grounds of the Ulster Folk Museum in Cultra. The text is very weathered but I think I could make out the word 'Armagh'.

gallery.filename: A village street scene at the Irish Folk Museum - geograph.org.uk - 1160477.jpg
gallery.title: File:A village street scene at the Irish Folk Museum - geograph.org.uk - 1160477.jpg
gallery.description: A village street scene at the Irish Folk Museum This jewel, near Ballycultra, is the most impressive museum of its kind in the British Isles. Real houses, cafes, shops, court, police station, churches, school and post office etc. etc. etc. Have been saved from demolition and removed stone by stone and built in this wonderful place. A veritable gem in Northern Ireland's crown. A must see experience.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.title: File:Irish Folk Museum, Ballycultra. - geograph.org.uk - 1160480.jpg
gallery.description: Irish Folk Museum, Ballycultra. A real church saved from demolition, removed, stone by stone, and rebuilt at the heritage centre. I think this was the Church of Ireland removed from Kilmore.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland
